messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points** | Topic | Summary | |-------|---------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the maximum speed you may drive.
• On highways, 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In residential areas, 25–35 mph.
• Speed limits can be lower during construction or adverse weather. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle up can result in a $100 fine. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑abuse treatment, and possible jail time.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Violations carry a $50 fine. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• At four‑way stops, the first vehicle to arrive has the right of way. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Failure to stop can lead to a $200 fine. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the lane is marked for left‑hand traffic. | | **Parking** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a no‑parking zone can result in a $100 fine. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Failure to register can lead to a $200 fine and possible towing. | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Cameras enforce speed limits, red‑light violations, and seat‑belt use.
• Infractions result in mailed tickets. | | **Special Rules for Commercial Vehicles** | • Commercial drivers must adhere to Hours‑of‑Service (HOS) regulations.
• Overspeeding, improper loading, and unsafe driving can lead to heavy penalties. | ### How to Find Specific Statutes - **Texas Transportation Code**: The primary source for all traffic laws. Available online at the Texas Legislature’s website. - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)**: Offers guides, FAQs, and downloadable handbooks. - **Legal Aid & Law Libraries**: For deeper research or case law references. ### Common Penalties | Offense | Typical Fine | Possible Additional Penalties | |---------|--------------|------------------------------| | Speeding (up to 20 mph over limit) | $100–$200 | Points on license, increased insurance | | Seat‑belt violation | $100 | Points on license | | Cell‑phone use | $50 | Points on license | | DUI | $500–$1,000 | License suspension, jail time, mandatory treatment | | Parking violations | $50–$200 | Vehicle impoundment | ### Tips for Compliance 1. **Always check posted signs** – speed limits and special rules can change. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Keep your registration and insurance documents in the vehicle**. 4. **Be mindful of school buses and construction zones**. 5. **If you receive a ticket, read the instructions carefully** – you can usually pay online or contest it in court. --- If you need more detailed information on a specific aspect (e.g., DUI statutes, commercial driver regulations, or how to contest a ticket), let me know!
